## Answers

**h01** — `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16-45`; work in `CheckAndPresign`, refreshing S3 pre‑signed attachment URLs and `payload.s3_object.last_presigned_time`) — once at startup, then every 12 h (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `runner.go:27`, ticker loop `runner.go:29-41`; entries re‑signed only when <4 days remain of the 5‑day expiry, `runner.go:85-91`) — wired in `Server.startBackgroundRunners`: constructed at `server/server.go:162`, immediate `RunOnce` at `server/server.go:163`, continuous goroutine at `server/server.go:166-171`, itself called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

**h02** — Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (the actual HTTP call is `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`; the async path enqueues via `PostAsync` `webhook.go:184` and 4 worker goroutines started in `init()` `webhook.go:42-55` call `Post`).
Protection: dial‑time SSRF guard — `safeClient`'s custom `Transport.DialContext = safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`, `safeDialContext` at `webhook.go:59-77`) which resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:44-50`) against `reservedCIDRs` (loopback, RFC‑1918, 169.254.0.0/16 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`). This also defeats DNS rebinding. A second, config‑time check is `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62-79`, scheme + resolved‑IP check). Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`) disables the check.

**r01** — Premise is wrong on both counts: there is no Redis anywhere in the repo (no `redis` string in any `.go` file or in `go.mod`). Caching is a hand-rolled **in-process, in-memory** cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`sync.Map` + TTL + a `cleanupLoop` goroutine, `cache.go:66-90`). The store creates three of them — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — in `store.New` at `store/store.go:38-58`, all with the same config: **DefaultTTL = 10 minutes**, CleanupInterval 5 min, MaxItems 1000 (`store/store.go:40-45`; same defaults in `cache.DefaultConfig()`, `store/cache/cache.go:57-64`). So user entries live 10 minutes; they are populated in `ListUsers`/`GetUser` (`store/user.go:143,167`) and explicitly invalidated on delete/update via `deleteUserCache` (`store/user_delete.go:39-47`).

**r02** — Premise is wrong: **there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase** — no per-user limiter, no `golang.org/x/time/rate`, no echo `middleware.RateLimiter`, and hence no request limits to report. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `rate.?limit` over `.go` files and `go.mod` yields exactly one hit, and it is a comment in a doc file listing an unimplemented idea: `internal/email/doc.go:86` ("Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse"). The Echo middleware chain is only `Recover()` and CORS (`server/server.go:50-51`); API access control is authentication/authorization via `Authorizer` (`server/router/api/v1/authz.go`), not throttling. The closest thing to load control is concurrency semaphores for thumbnail/image work (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`) and the bounded 128-slot webhook queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: **no cron scheduler is running and no nightly database-cleanup job exists**, so there is no scheduled time. The `internal/scheduler` package is a self-contained, unused library — `scheduler.New`, `Register`, and `Start` are called only from its own tests and examples (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `integration_test.go`); a grep for `internal/scheduler` imports across non-test code returns nothing. The "daily-cleanup" at `0 2 * * *` you may have seen is illustrative documentation in the package doc comment (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:15-20`), not a registered job. The only real periodic work is the S3 presign runner on a plain `time.Ticker` every 12 h (see h01, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41`, wired at `server/server.go:162-171`).

**r04** — Premise is wrong: **neither** — there is no message broker at all. No NATS, RabbitMQ, or AMQP dependency appears in `go.mod` or any `.go` file, and no queue is declared anywhere. Webhook delivery is entirely in-process: a buffered Go channel `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by **4 goroutines** started in the package `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `webhook.Post` (`webhook.go:120`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`webhook.go:184-196`), which drops the payload with a warning if the channel is full. Consequence worth noting: the queue is unbounded-loss and non-durable — pending webhooks are lost on restart.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: **there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server** in this repo (no `graphql` string in any `.go` file or in `go.mod`). The public API is defined by **Protocol Buffers** under `proto/api/v1/` — `memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `common.proto` — with Go code generated into `proto/gen/api/v1` (and Connect stubs in `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect`). It is exposed over Connect RPC + gRPC‑Gateway REST, registered by `(*APIV1Service).RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65`, wired at `server/server.go:89`). Additional non-RPC surfaces: HTTP file serving under `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), an MCP server with an OpenAPI description (`server/router/mcp/`, incl. `openapi.go`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:63`).
